strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with per-iteration scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, where each iteration computes block-wise mean-square scaling factors from the previous result, applies them, all-reduces, then un-scales. This is the reference approach with 8 all-reduce dispatches (plus 1 initial) = 9 total. Minimizes algorithmic complexity at the cost of maximum latency from sequential dependencies.

strategies.name: Fused buffer all-reduce with vectorized scaling
strategies.desc: Concatenates all 8 iteration buffers into a single tensor of shape (8, 4096) and issues a single all-reduce per iteration on the full working state, eliminating per-block multiplications inside the collective. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches but with larger payloads (32KB vs 4KB), trading bandwidth for fewer synchronization points and better amortization of collective latency overhead.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather pipeline
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter (scattering 8 blocks across ranks) followed by local computation on owned shard, then all-gather to reconstruct full result. At world size 224, each rank computes scaling factors for ~0.036 blocks worth of data, enabling 16 total dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but with 224x smaller per-rank computation and potential for overlapping communication with local ops on other iterations.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce (smaller world size, lower latency) followed by inter-node all-reduce on node representatives. For 224 ranks this could be 28 nodes × 8 devices, giving 2×8=16 dispatches with significantly reduced per-dispatch latency on the intra-node phase, amortizing the alpha term in the cost model.

strategies.name: Pipelined block-parallel all-reduce with staggered start
strategies.desc:
Issues all 8 iterations' all-reduce operations asynchronously without waiting for previous iteration completion, using distinct buffer allocations per iteration. Dependencies are enforced only through the scaling-factor computation chain, allowing network hardware to pipeline up to 8 in-flight collectives simultaneously. Total 8 dispatches but with overlapped execution hiding per-dispatch alpha+beta latency behind computation and other transfers.
